question: Bind — ATK, 3v2 man-advantage, 1:09 left, no spike planted. You and your Omen ally are pushing through A Bath toward A Site — 'A Site: 9m' proximity label visible. One defender is alive ahead on A Site, one is unaccounted for. How do you push through A Bath as the advantage team?

options.label: Stagger the push — Omen goes first to absorb or bait the angle while you trail 2-3m behind to trade instantly if he takes a bullet
options.explication_courte: In a 3v2 you already win if you don't throw it. Staggering the push means the defender can only shoot one of you at a time — you are the trade. If Omen is shot, you swing and kill the now-low, reloading defender. You convert a 3v2 into a clean 2v1.

sources_option.citation: Playing trade positions behind an entry keeps a man-advantage intact; both players rushing the same angle at once means one bullet can kill both in a crossfire

options.label: Both rush out together at the same instant to overwhelm the defender with two targets
options.explication_courte: Rushing two bodies through the same tight choke at once can clip both players with one spray — the defender stacks one gun on the door and gets a double. Staggered entries prevent a multi-kill from a single pre-aimed hold.

sources_option.citation: Funnelling two players through the same chokepoint simultaneously lets a holding defender hit both; stagger to force separate duels

options.label: Have Omen use his smoke to blind the A Site angle, then both enter under the smoke together
options.explication_courte: Smoking the A Site angle is a valid tool to neutralise the known defender before entry. The risk is that the second unaccounted defender may be watching a different entrance that the smoke doesn't cover — and spending Omen's smoke early leaves you without it for the actual plant/post-plant.

sources_option.citation: Utility used for entry is expended and unavailable for post-plant; weigh the cost of spending smoke before the duel vs the advantage it creates

options.label: Stop at A Bath and wait for the third teammate to catch up before entering — use full numbers
options.explication_courte: Stopping to wait in a corridor at 1:09 with two defenders alive burns the clock and gives the defense time to regroup, set up crossfires, and potentially retake B to catch the third teammate from behind. In a 3v2 with map pressure you already have the winning hand — play it now.

sources_option.citation: Delaying an attack to consolidate numbers at low time lets defenders reset and cross-map — act on your advantage before it evaporates

explication_longue: A 3v2 ATK advantage in A Bath with A Site 9 metres ahead is a round you can only lose by over-thinking or by stacking both bodies into the same angle. The correct push is staggered: Omen moves first through the corridor while you trail 2-3 metres behind with your crosshair already on the line the defender holds. If the defender shoots Omen, you are the instant trade — you swing, he's reloading or repositioning off the kill, and your Spectre punishes the exposed moment. You've just converted a 3v2 into a 2v1 with a fresh gun and full HP. Rushing through together at the same instant collapses two players into a single bottleneck — a well-placed defender can hit both with one spray if they're stacked too tight. Waiting for the third man sounds safe but burns your clock at 1:09 in a round where you have the numbers edge; defenders use that pause to reset crossfires, and the second unaccounted defender may rotate behind your third teammate. Using Omen's smoke to cover the A Site angle before entry is defensible — it removes the known threat — but it spends a key post-plant tool early and leaves the unaccounted second defender unchecked on another line. Stagger, trade, win.

sources.citation: Stagger entry to force separate duels and keep the trade chain intact — rushing side-by-side risks a single hold killing both
